title: Connection reuse exists because handshakes are expensive
body: Opening TCP plus TLS costs round trips and CPU before a byte of content moves; keep-alive and connection pools amortise that across many requests. On high-latency links the handshake, not the payload, dominates small API calls. Half of performance engineering is refusing to pay introductions repeatedly.
source_hint: RFC 9112 connection reuse; TLS handshake costs
